author: Dawn Forrest
title: Community colleges aim to fill regional healthcare gap with EMT program - NewsBreak
text:
By Dawn Forrest WFXR image ,
1 hours ago
ROANOKE, Va. ( WFXR ) – As the need for health care workers in our region continues to swell, a new community college partnership aims to train Emergency Medical Technicians (EMTs) and close the gap.
New River Community College (NRCC), Central Virginia Community College (CVCC) and Virginia Western Community College (VWCC) are teaming up to offer an Advanced Emergency Medical Technician (AEMT) program.
School representatives say the program is short-term, non-credit and takes EMTs to a higher level of prehospital care. Students learn patient assessment, airway management, medication administration and more.
Every student who tested for the National Registry Advanced EMT certification this year has passed. In addition, NRCC’s inaugural AEMT cohort achieved a 100 percent course pass rate.
Ross Matney, NRCC’s workforce training coordinator, says these numbers stem from strong partnership and student dedication.
“The success of this program highlights the impact we can have when we partner together to meet the needs of our communities,” Matney said. “We’re proud of our students for their hard work and commitment, and we appreciate the collaboration that has helped expand access to this valuable training for EMS professionals across our region.”
Educators say helping EMTs grow in their career also boosts retention in our region’s hospitals, creating greater access to healthcare.
“By investing in the education of our EMS professionals, we’re investing in the health and safety of the communities they serve,” said Matney.
